image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of two sea lions resting on a wooden dock structure near water. The primary subject is a large male sea lion in the foreground right, characterized by dark brown, wet-looking fur and a prominent sagittal crest. A second, lighter brown sea lion (likely female or juvenile) is visible in the background left, resting its head near the male's shoulder. The background consists of blurred wooden planks and hints of blue water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad with prominent sagittal crest in males.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreground subject clearly displays the characteristic bulge on the top of the skull (sagittal crest) typical of adult male sea lions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: External ear pinnae (visible ear flaps) distinguish from true seals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Small but distinct external ear flaps are visible on the side of the foreground sea lion's head, confirming it is an otariid (sea lion/fur seal) and not a phocid (true seal).
Stiff, light-colored whiskers are clearly visible protruding from the snout area of both animals.
